title: sqlguardllm policy
description: What SQL written by an untrusted source may do. See https://github.com/jmmana/sqlguardllm/blob/main/docs/DESIGN.md

dialect.description: Dialect of the SQL to check: postgres, mysql, tsql, oracle, sqlite…

tables.description: Allowlisted tables, optionally qualified (sales.customers). null disables the allowlist, which is not recommended.

hidden_columns.description: Columns that may never be referenced, as table.column.

row_filters.description: Table → boolean SQL condition with {context.path} placeholders.

max_rows.description: Maximum rows a query may return. null disables the limit.

default_schema.description: Schema assumed for unqualified table references.

denied_functions.description: Replaces the built-in denylist for the dialect when given.

max_joins.description: Maximum joins in the whole query.

max_subquery_depth.description: Maximum nesting of subqueries, derived tables and CTEs.

forbid_cartesian.description: Reject CROSS JOIN and comma joins with no linking equality in WHERE.

required_filters.description: Table → columns; every read of the table must filter on one of them.

output_dialect.description: Generate the rewritten SQL in this dialect instead of dialect.

masked_columns.description: table.column → mask. Selectable but masked; never usable in filters, joins, grouping or ordering.

aggregate_only.description: Table → minimum group size k: only aggregates, groups of at least k rows.

schema.description: Table → columns. Lets * over a table with masked columns be expanded.

lint_suppress.description: sqlguardllm lint warning code → why it doesn't apply to this policy. Only the linter reads it.
